rationale: The literature provided does not support a dichotomous genotype-phenotype segregation rule wherein complete anterior pituitary aplasia is restricted to biallelic null/frameshift variants while structural hypoplasia is confined to splice-site or in-frame hypomorphic alleles. Instead, systematic reviews and developmental genetics studies (e.g., Lodge et al., 2024; Cullingford, 2023; Hage et al., 2021) document anterior pituitary aplasia and hypoplasia along a shared phenotypic spectrum of primary ciliary and Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) pathway disruption. Across available cohorts and reviews, pituitary findings in TBC1D32-related congenital hypopituitarism are described collectively as aplasia or hypoplasia without reliable segregation by variant class.

evidence.text: Variants in TBC1D32 disrupt ciliary function and SHH signaling necessary for pituitary specification, manifesting as either a hypoplastic or absent pituitary gland in humans without established allelic segregation.

conflicts: Literature reviews and cohort summaries report variable expressivity (both aplasia and hypoplasia) across ciliary gene defects and within identical mutations, arguing against an absolute segregation between null variants causing aplasia and hypomorphic variants causing hypoplasia.

The total number of reported individuals with biallelic TBC1D32 pathogenic variants is extremely low, making statistically validated genotype-phenotype correlations between variant classes currently unproven.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual ciliogenesis and SHH signaling activity in patient-derived fibroblasts or CRISPR knock-in cell lines correlate quantitatively with remaining anterior pituitary volume on volumetric 3T brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing the downstream signaling defect in vitro can determine whether the degree of hypoplasia vs. aplasia is truly allele-specific or influenced by developmental stochasticity and genetic modifiers.

new_directions.question_text: What is the complete clinical and neuroimaging distribution across all worldwide reported TBC1D32 families when standardized high-resolution pituitary protocol MRI images are centrally re-reviewed?
new_directions.rationale: High-resolution re-review of neuroimaging across all documented pedigrees is required to definitively ascertain whether any true residual anterior pituitary tissue is present in reported cases of presumed aplasia.
